findings.text: Per-vCPU synthetic timer state bundles a high-resolution timer with its index, configuration union, current count and expiry time, plus a pending message buffer and a flag indicating a message awaits delivery.

Per-vCPU synthetic interrupt controller state holds version, control, message page and event page values, an array of interrupt states with per-entry routing, fixed-size bitmaps covering 256 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::kvm_vcpu_hv_synic L43-54] vectors each for automatic end-of-interrupt and vector presence, plus active and page-preservation flags.

Each Hyper-V TLB flush queue pairs a write-side spinlock with a kernel FIFO of guest physical entries, sized to 16 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::KVM_HV_TLB_FLUSH_FIFO_SIZE L57-57] slots, with a queue per nested level tracked by an enumeration that also provides a count.

Per-vCPU Hyper-V state links back to the owning vCPU, records virtual processor index, virtual APIC address and runtime offset, embeds synthetic controller and exit buffers with a timer array and pending bitmap and a CPUID enforcement flag, caches feature and enlightenment and debug and nested leaf values, provides flush queues with sparse-bank and mask scratch space, stores a VP assist page copy, and tracks nested page and identity values.

Flush queue depth is 16 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::KVM_HV_TLB_FLUSH_FIFO_SIZE L57-57] entries, while the full-flush sentinel uses all bits set [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::KVM_HV_TLB_FLUSHALL_ENTRY L66-77] to distinguish global invalidation from address-specific entries.

Signature leaf reports 0x31237648 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HYPERV_CPUID_SIGNATURE_EAX L121-121], with debug leaves at 0x40000080 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HYPERV_CPUID_SYNDBG_VENDOR_AND_MAX_FUNCTIONS L129-131], 0x40000081 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HYPERV_CPUID_SYNDBG_INTERFACE L129-131] and 0x40000082 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HYPERV_CPUID_SYNDBG_PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES L129-131].

Kernel-debugging capability uses BIT macro argument 1 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_SYNDBG_CAP_ALLOW_KERNEL_DEBUGGING L137-137], while hypercall-based debug transport uses BIT macro argument 2 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_SYNDBG_OPTION_USE_HCALLS L148-148].

Debug MSRs are 0x400000F1 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_MSR_SYNDBG_CONTROL L140-145] for control, 0x400000F2 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_MSR_SYNDBG_STATUS L140-145] for status, 0x400000F3 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_MSR_SYNDBG_SEND_BUFFER L140-145] for send, 0x400000F4 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_MSR_SYNDBG_RECV_BUFFER L140-145] for receive, 0x400000F5 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_MSR_SYNDBG_PENDING_BUFFER L140-145] for pending, and 0x400000FF [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.h::HV_X64_MSR_SYNDBG_OPTIONS L140-145] for options.

Counter access modes are 1 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_LSB L49-266] for low byte, 2 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_MSB L49-266] for high byte, 3 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_WORD0 L49-266] for word low phase and 4 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_WORD1 L49-266] for word high phase.

Implement-limits leaf reports the maximum virtual processor count with 64 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.c::kvm_hv_eventfd_assign L2894-2945] logical processors matching a recent Hyper-V release, nested leaf merges version with direct-flush and bitmap flags in a return register and performance-control in another, debug vendor leaf clears max function while spreading a fixed vendor signature across registers, interface leaf presents a fixed interface signature, capability leaf adds kernel-debugging allowance, unlisted leaves leave entries unchanged, and final tables are copied to user memory with fault status on failure.

Request helper tests and clears a per-vCPU flag under atomic semantics with an ordering barrier before reporting success, applies a mask to the request index when clearing, and forbids the dead-VM request via a compile-time check, ensuring a dead VM stays dead.

Hypercall handling is enabled only when the arch flag is set and a guest OS identifier is present, with a disabled build always reporting false and returning an access-denied status for hypercalls, automatic end-of-interrupt reflects the per-vector bitmap when per-vCPU state exists else false, and nested flush support is read from cached nested feature flags.

Assist verification succeeds immediately when per-vCPU state is absent or the assist page is disabled, otherwise it fetches the page, nested transitions re-raise a flush request when per-vCPU state exists and hardware-assisted paging is enabled so the correct per-level queue is rechecked after a level change, timing and init helpers are no-ops in this configuration, and queue purge discards pending entries after consuming its request while the disabled variant does nothing.

Elapsed-time helper returns no progress when the period is unset, otherwise derives progress from remaining time for the timer channel and from load timestamps for other channels, count and output helpers scale elapsed time by the PIT frequency into ticks and apply per-mode wrapping and level rules for mode values from 0 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_LSB L49-266] to 5 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_LSB L49-266], and gate helper restarts counting on rising edges for retriggerable and periodic families while leaving terminal-count families unaffected.

Count latch captures the current counter until consumed and status latch packs output with access and mode and BCD flags until consumed, acknowledgment path marks the interrupt as acked with ordering before checking pending work and re-queues the worker when ticks remain, migration pins ownership to the boot vCPU with the state mutex held around timer restart, and worker skips delivery when reinject is armed but unacked, otherwise pulses the PIT line and fans out a watchdog NMI when virtual-wire mode is active.

GSI mapping walks the routing table under read-side protection and copies matching entries for the caller, while IRQ setting maps the line then invokes each mapped chip handler and sums successes, reporting failure when no handler accepts the line, thereby driving both legacy and modern controllers without probing which the guest uses.

Timer callback bumps pending when reinject is armed, queues the worker, and restarts for periodic mode while stopping otherwise, reset clears pending and marks acked, and reinject toggling avoids redundant work, inhibits hardware APIC acceleration while armed, registers acknowledgment and mask notifiers, preserves initial state, and requests an IOAPIC rescan when the IOAPIC is in kernel.

Timer creation skips when the IOAPIC is not in kernel or HPET legacy is flagged, otherwise cancels any prior timer, converts the count to an interval, clamps small periodic intervals to a host minimum with rate-limited notice, and starts an absolute timer, count value 0 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::create_pit_timer L322-482] maps to 0x10000 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::create_pit_timer L322-482], the timer channel selects non-periodic versus periodic versus disabled by mode while other channels only timestamp loads, HPET legacy path briefly disables the timer around reload, and port writes validate range with unsupported status on miss, mask data to byte width, and decode read-back versus counter-select with latch or mode programming.

Flush-queue write lock serializes concurrent producers from other vCPUs, while the consumer path first consumes its request flag with ordering, selects the queue for the current nested level, and discards entries, with level transitions re-raising the request so async puts are not lost.

PIT state mutex guards timer migration, port writes and count loads with an assertion that loaders hold it, IRQ mutex guards acknowledgment and mask notifier list updates while readers use read-side protection, removal synchronizes before returning, and routing lookups run inside read-side sections with fallback when no table or entry exists.

Counter modes from 0 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_LSB L49-266] to 5 [CITED arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c::RW_STATE_LSB L49-266] define terminal-count versus retriggerable versus rate and square periodic families, with gate edges reloading timestamps for retriggerable and periodic members, expiry wrapping to the top of the counter range, and loads arming the timer per family.

Read-back commands latch count or status per channel until consumed, counter-select either latches immediately when access is cleared or programs access with read and write phases plus mode and BCD, and timer plus reinject plus acknowledgment plus worker form a coalescing loop where pending ticks wait for ack before delivery resumes.

Cached CPUID values gate feature visibility, with unlisted debug leaves leaving entries unchanged, and flush handling moves through request, per-level queueing, and purge on entry or level change, ensuring the queue matching the current level is the one drained.

User-table copy failure yields a fault status, tiny periodic intervals are clamped to a host minimum to avoid scheduler overload, square-mode odd counts and strobe precision are noted approximate, null-count reporting is unimplemented, absent per-vCPU or APIC or PIT state safely skips work, out-of-range ports are rejected, and the dead-VM request is forbidden at compile time.
Logging prefix macro scopes driver messages under the module name.
Modulo helper ships in division-based and native variants to cover builds with and without fast wide remainder support.
Header uses an include guard to prevent multiple inclusion.
